title: Map domain errors to HTTP responses in one place
body:
Adds a single exception handler that maps `app.errors.DomainError` subclasses to status codes, and makes `capture_charge` validate status/amount with domain errors.

Before this, a mix of handlers caught errors and built responses by hand, and 409 vs 422 was inconsistent across endpoints (API-41).
author: carol

@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
+from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
+
+from app import errors
+from app.utils.logging import get_logger
+
+log = get_logger(__name__)
+
+_STATUS = {
+    errors.NotFound: 404,
+    errors.Conflict: 409,
+    errors.PaymentDeclined: 402,
+    errors.RefundExceedsCapture: 422,
+    errors.ProviderUnavailable: 503,
+}
+
+
+def register(app: FastAPI) -> None:
+    @app.exception_handler(errors.DomainError)
+    async def _domain_error(request: Request, exc: errors.DomainError) -> JSONResponse:
+        status = _STATUS.get(type(exc), 400)
+        log.warning("domain_error", code=exc.code, path=request.url.path, status=status)
+        return JSONResponse({"error": {"code": exc.code, "message": str(exc)}}, status_code=status)
